teams.heading: Henry Pollock hat-trick headlines England's 73-8 rout of Fiji in July
teams.body: Henry Pollock scored a second-half hat-trick as England ran in 11 tries to beat Fiji 73-8 in July, ending a five-Test losing run of their own. Fiji, ranked 10th in the world, have lost four of five Tests this year. Jake White, the former Bulls director of rugby, takes charge with his first match against Japan still to come, followed by November Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: The only men's 15s item on the shortlist that is not a repeat of the Jake White story already run on this tab.

teams.heading: Club: George Hendy stars as Northampton end England's Champions Cup duck
teams.body: In club rugby, Northampton beat Cardiff 28-12 to deliver the first Premiership win of the Champions Cup's opening round, after seven English rivals had failed to claim one. Uncapped winger George Hendy set up the opening try with an aerial catch and run from halfway and touched down again in the second half. Director of rugby Phil Dowson said, "George can break the game open," while England's scrum-half Alex Mitchell also caught Planet Rugby's eye ahead of the November squad announcement.

lead.why: The freshest men's club item with a clear England selection hook, since Hendy and Mitchell are both being watched ahead of the November squad.

teams.heading: Montpellier club grind Bath down 32-14 in Champions Cup opener
teams.body: Top 14 club Montpellier came from four points down at the break to beat Bath 32-14 at a sold-out Recreation Ground on the Champions Cup's opening weekend. Bath were outscored 22-0 after half-time, Adam Hastings having kept the visitors within range with a first-half penalty. Montpellier took the win on grit and guile, and were beaten finalists in the Top 14 last season.

teams.heading: Munster club: Tadhg Beirne hails Foley tribute win as "exactly the performance"
teams.body: Munster's Champions Cup win over Racing 92 in Cork was a club occasion with a deep emotional thread: skipper Tadhg Beirne said the 33-25 victory was "exactly the performance" Anthony Foley would have been proud of, a decade after Foley died on the eve of the Racing match in Paris. Olive Foley presented the jerseys on Friday. Twenty-year-old Charlie O'Shea made his first Champions Cup start at No. 10 and contributed six points.

lead.why: The only new men's item in the shortlist about an Ireland-qualified player that is not already covered, and the strongest one available.

teams.heading: Italy's highest world ranking is No. 8, reached in 2007 and 2024
teams.body: Italy's highest world ranking is No. 8, reached in 2007 and 2024. In their three Nations Championship matches so far, Italy have lost all three. They have scored 37 points and conceded 131, a points difference of -94. The most recent result was a 57-10 defeat to Australia in Round 3. Next up is South Africa in Round 4.

teams.heading: Scotland's biggest win in their last 11 Tests: 56-0 over Tonga
teams.body: Across their last 11 Tests, Scotland have scored 348 points. In the same 11 matches they have conceded 299, which works out at 31.6 points scored and 27.2 conceded a game. The biggest win in that window was a 56-0 victory over Tonga, a home International Friendly played in November 2025, and it stands as the widest winning margin across those matches.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie takes TMO row to World Rugby's November officials meeting
teams.body: Dave Rennie is reported to be raising the TMO controversy at World Rugby's November officials meeting, which sits inside a review of TMO protocols following recent test controversies. Argentina have a stake in that debate: the BBC headlined its report of the 24-31 Round 3 defeat to England 'Chaos' & 'comedy refereering'. The review stays open until World Rugby issues new guidance or concludes it after November, and one ESPN headline frames the task as fixing the protocol before the 2027 World Cup.

teams.heading: Ewen McKenzie says Les Kiss' hand was forced before Bledisloe II
teams.body: Ewen McKenzie, a former Wallabies head coach, was far from confident of Australia's chances before last Saturday's second Bledisloe Test, saying Les Kiss' hand had been forced by injuries. Len Ikitau was ruled out with a concussion and Ben Donaldson was hurt in the build-up, which pushed Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i into midfield and left the fly-half spot unsettled. McKenzie said the Wallabies had half a dozen fly-half candidates, none with much experience. Australia went on to lose 43-21.

lead.why: A former Wallabies coach's critique of Les Kiss' selections is a different angle from the Sydney mauling and the 22-0 reaction already covered today.

teams.heading: Club: Springboks prospect Cheswill Jooste hat-trick fires Bulls past Stade Français
teams.body: Club: the Bulls' Champions Cup opener belonged to Cheswill Jooste, the 20-year-old wing who scored a hat-trick in Saturday's 56-20 win over Stade Français. He was over inside half a minute, collecting a Harold Vorster kick, and completed his treble with a walk-in in the 73rd minute. Handré Pollard converted all eight tries, with Cobus Wiese, Cameron Hanekom, Marco van Staden, Jeandre Rudolph and Jan-Hendrik Wessels also crossing. Planet Rugby describes Jooste as a 'hot' Springboks prospect.

lead.why: It is a South Africa-linked story with a clear event, a named Springboks prospect and a hat-trick, and it is not one of the stories already run this week.
